tasks.task: Turn one procedure into on-the-job training

items.when: When there is a written procedure and a shift lead must teach it and sign people off
When the job lives in someone's head and must be written down before you can teach it
When a skill needs breaking into a few steps, each with a common mistake and a self-check
When learners must move from watching a full example to doing the procedure alone
When you start from a spoken description and need the procedure, a gap check and a deck in one run
When the module is drafted, to find where it asks learners to hold too much at once

tasks.task: Plan a training session with timings and practice

items.when: When a manager asks for training on one task and you need the steps from request to proof it worked
When you have a skills gap and need objectives, a session outline and a coaching plan for after
When you know the skill, group and time and need the session planned minute by minute
When you want a second design that starts from the work problem, to compare with your outline
Before the session runs, to cut overload, fix barriers and add quick checks of who has got it
When the session is all talk and needs one repeatable task, a clear standard and fast feedback

tasks.task: Decide whether a request is really a training problem

items.when: When a manager asks for training on something and you doubt that skill is the cause
When the same error keeps coming back and you need a chain of whys checked against facts
When the cause must be found with the team in a room, without it turning into blame

tasks.task: Build a week-by-week onboarding path for one role

items.when: When you hire the same role again and again and want new starters doing the job alone sooner
When week one needs a day-by-day plan with one small real task and who they meet
When each new hire needs clear goals for day 30, 60 and 90
When the starters are volunteers and you need an induction, a practice plan and supervision gaps
Each week after the start date, to check progress against the path and say what to fix

tasks.task: Plan a workshop with an agenda and facilitator guide

items.when: When a workshop must end with a decision, a plan or a practised skill, in a room or online
When the workshop is for a charity or community group and needs activities, worksheets and host notes
When the session is online and one-to-many, to get a teaching outline and a slide brief
When a leadership team talks over each other and quiet people never get to think aloud

tasks.task: Write up a workshop or meeting from rough notes

items.when: When you have typed or photographed notes and need decisions, owners and dates on one page
When the session was recorded and you need a transcript, a summary and notes

tasks.task: Write a one-page job aid, handout or reference card

items.when: When you have session notes or slides and need one page people can use at the station a month on
When a step is easier shown than told, to plan the diagram that sits beside the words
When the page is drafted, to find where it is too crowded to use mid-task

tasks.task: Write a quiz or knowledge check with an answer key

items.when: When you need short recall questions at easy, medium and hard levels on one topic
When the quiz should come with the explanation, worked examples and practice it tests
When answers are written or practical and markers need a description of each level
Before anyone sits it, to check the quiz tests the stated goals and marks fairly
When the check is a tick-box at the end and should be recall that makes the learning stick

tasks.task: Build a competency sign-off checklist and observation form

items.when: When the sign-off must match the goals and steps of one procedure
When "can do the job" is vague and must become things an observer can see and tick
When someone will watch the task or the trainer and needs look-fors and a sheet to record facts

tasks.task: Design practice tasks and role-plays for one skill

items.when: When you have one good example and need staged practice that takes the help away bit by bit
When people pass the drill and you need new cases that test the skill on real, messier work
When the skill is a people skill and you need a practice activity with evidence to collect
When practice is just repetition and needs a target a little past what people can do now

tasks.task: Build a training deck from a procedure or session plan

items.when: When you have an outline or document and need a clean deck for the room
When the client's trainers must edit the slides in PowerPoint afterwards
When you want two or three draft decks from the same outline to compare before you commit
When slides are drafted, to find the ones that carry too much text or too many ideas
Before the deck goes out, to check speaker notes, links and that it reads without you

tasks.task: Build a skills matrix and read the gap report

items.when: When a team needs its skills listed, rated by self and manager, and the thin spots shown
When no one has written what good looks like at each level for the roles in the matrix

tasks.task: Write a career ladder and promotion criteria

items.when: When the ladder must be built from the same skills and levels the team is already rated on
When one job family needs levels, growth plans and a guide for managers' career talks
When a real promotion case is due, to match the person's evidence to the criteria and list gaps
When the ladder must feed review forms, goal templates and a fair rating meeting

tasks.task: Write development plans for named people

items.when: When each person's plan should point at the next level on their ladder
When growth depends on pairing people up and you need matching rules and talk guides
When a plan reads as a verdict on the person and should name strategies to try next

tasks.task: Run a training needs analysis from surveys and reviews

items.when: When you have goals, survey exports, review themes and error data and need counted skill gaps
When there is no data yet and you need survey questions and a focus group guide
Before you count the answers, to find questions whose results cannot be trusted
When leaders want the survey findings in a briefing with honest caveats on who answered
For each gap on the list, to drop the ones training will not fix

tasks.task: Write the annual learning plan, calendar and budget

items.when: When next year's goals or budget are set, or a board asks what training should buy
Before the plan, so every line traces to a counted gap and not a course catalogue
When you need the training spend phased by month and team, with a way to report variance
When the plan goes to a board and must ask for a clear decision with the evidence mapped

tasks.task: Compare training providers or learning tools

items.when: When you hold two or three provider quotes and need cost, risks and a clear pick
When several providers must be scored against weighted needs so the choice can be defended

tasks.task: Plan and run the evaluation of a training programme

items.when: Before a programme launches, to fix the expected result, its baseline and what to measure when
When one programme must be followed from launch to a go, fix or stop call
Some weeks after a course, to compare real work with the skills taught
When you need the reaction and follow-up questions for learners and their managers

tasks.task: Plan follow-up so skills stick after the session

items.when: When topics must come back at widening gaps over the weeks after training
When each follow-up needs a two-minute recall quiz, not a re-read of the slides
When managers should raise the new skill in weekly one-on-ones with praise and one thing to fix
When the plan is one big session and nothing after, to spread it out and add recall

tasks.task: Set up an apprentice skills log, weekly plan and mentor guide

items.when: When you take on an apprentice or trainee and need a year-one log, weekly plan and mentor guide
When a senior person is good at the job but cannot explain it in steps a beginner can follow
When mentors need a six-month plan and guides for their talks with the apprentice
When sign-off levels are vague, to make each one something the mentor can see

tasks.task: Build a training pack for a new software system

items.when: When staff must use a new till, booking, CRM or accounts system in week one
Before go-live, to list open blockers and record a go or no-go call
When staff are nervous or resistant and you need a stakeholder map and message plan
When the same how-do-I questions keep coming and need short searchable answers
When the switch needs an announcement, FAQ and manager talking points
A few weeks after go-live, to see who is using the new way and what is in the way

tasks.task: Script short how-to videos

items.when: When a written guide should become narrated slides and a voice-over video
Before scripting, to cut the task into the few steps one short video can carry
When nobody wants to be on camera and a presenter video must be made from the script
When a screen recording needs trimming, captions and mistakes cut by editing the text

tasks.task: Design manager and leadership training

items.when: When managers need one practical session with a practice activity, not a slide talk
When the job is a whole programme with a 360 form and a coaching guide
When the skill to teach is feedback and managers need a script to ask for it and give it
When managers avoid hard feedback or give it harshly and need a way to be clear and kind

tasks.task: Roll out required training on a policy or safety rule

items.when: When an approved policy must be explained to staff in plain words with what changes for them
When staff must be told the training is due, with talking points for their managers
When you need proof people understood the rule, not only that they attended
On a schedule, to catch training that still teaches an old version of the policy

always.when: Before any training document goes out, to catch typos and terms spelt two ways
When training states a rule, number or legal duty you cannot trace to the client's own source

helpers.when: When the job is a full e-learning course with storyboards and branching scenarios
When the procedure or system guide does not exist yet and must be written first
When promotion, pay or performance rules sit behind the ladder or the development plans
When the deck or handout must look finished and on brand, not only be clear
When a rollout needs a staff message plan beyond one announcement
When how-to videos need filming, editing and captions, not only scripts

gaps: No library item builds a skills matrix or rating sheet; only the kit skill covers it
No library item writes an individual development plan for a named person from their ratings
No library item writes a one-page job aid or quick reference card for a station or a software screen
No library item writes role-play scripts with a customer brief, an observer sheet and debrief questions
No library item plans a workshop run sheet and kit list, or an online whiteboard layout
No library item gives clearly different workshop designs to compare for one goal
No library item writes a how-to or screen-recording video script with captions for staff training
No library item writes an end-of-course reaction form or a manager follow-up form
No library item works out what a training programme returned against its cost
No library item covers apprentices: a skills log, off-the-job hours or a progress report for the provider
No library item tracks required training: who is due, who is overdue and what proof is held
No library item writes a full e-learning lesson or short microlearning units from source material
No library item interviews an expert to capture how they do a job for training; the one found writes AI agent files
No library item builds a training calendar for the year from the plan
